newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals seen opening lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals seen opening lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were seen opening lower Tuesday, in line with the bullion market overnight, where gold and silver gave back some of Monday's gains, and platinum group metals fell after confirmation Russia would resume exports of platinum and palladium soon.
COMEX June gold was seen opening unchanged to down 50 cents from Monday's close at $348.70 an ounce, after trading in a $349.10-348.00 range in overnight ACCESS trade.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $347.00/50 early, compared to the London Tuesday morning fix at $347.30 an ounce, and the New York close Monday around $347.40/90.
COMEX gold stocks fell 8,589 ounces Monday to 901,495 ounces, while COMEX silver stocks fell 279,526 ounces to 190,597,224 ounces.
COMEX July silver was seen opening unchanged to down 0.2 cent from the previous close at $4.835 an ounce, after trading a $4.855-4.840 range in ACCESS.
COMEX gold and silver prices recovered to their highest levels in a month intraday Monday before, giving back the gains by the close.

NYMEX July platinum was seen opening down $1.00 to $2.00 an ounce from Monday's close at $391.10 an ounce, while NYMEX June palladium was also seen down $1.00 to $2.00 an ounce from the close at $171.85 Tuesday.

Overnight officials Russia's metal export agency, Almaz, said talks with customers supplied under long term contract had resumed and PGM exports would resume in June, with enough metal to meet customer demand and keep prices at reasonable levels.
Russian PGM exports have been disrupted since December.
